memory_annotations.evidence_summary: For this Nashville workshop, Maya rejected an after-midnight connecting itinerary, compared two feasible Monday nonstops and two Thursday returns, and retained two round trips using the 6:10 p.m. outbound. The $552 itinerary with the 5:12 p.m. return is preferred, while the $575 itinerary with the 7:38 p.m. return remains as the higher-margin alternative. Nothing was booked.

messages.content: I need flights for a Nashville workshop. It starts Tuesday, April 20 at 9:00 a.m. and ends Thursday, April 22 at 2:30 p.m. I can leave Minneapolis after 3:30 Monday. Economy airfare needs to stay under $670.

I’ll compare Monday evening arrivals and Thursday returns with enough time for the trip between the client site and BNA. Is the workshop downtown, and will you be leaving directly from the client site Thursday?
Yes, it’s near Music Row. I’ll have my luggage with me Thursday and can leave as soon as the workshop ends.

From Music Row, I’d allow about 25–35 minutes to BNA in ordinary afternoon traffic, plus some buffer for pickup. Leaving at 2:30 would likely put you at the terminal around 3:10–3:25. I found three relevant Monday options: a 4:35 p.m. nonstop arriving 6:42 p.m. for $618 round trip, a 6:10 p.m. nonstop arriving 8:17 p.m. for $552, and a $431 itinerary connecting in Chicago that arrives at 12:24 a.m. Tuesday.
Drop the connection. Arriving after midnight before a 9:00 workshop isn’t useful.

Agreed. Both nonstops leave enough time to get to a Music Row hotel Monday evening. The 4:35 departure has only a 65-minute margin after your stated 3:30 availability, while the 6:10 departure is easier to make and still gets you to the hotel around 9:00 p.m.
What are the Thursday choices? I don’t want a flight that requires leaving before the workshop is done.

The earliest workable nonstop departs BNA at 5:12 p.m. and arrives MSP at 7:23 p.m. It gives roughly 1 hour 45 minutes at the airport if you reach the terminal by 3:25. A later nonstop leaves at 7:38 p.m. and arrives at 9:49 p.m., giving considerably more margin. There is also a 4:18 p.m. departure, but reaching it would be too tight after a 2:30 finish, so I excluded it.
Can either Monday flight pair with either of those returns? Show me the useful combinations and total prices.

Yes. The four combinations are: 4:35 p.m. Monday with 5:12 p.m. Thursday for $618; 4:35 with 7:38 for $641; 6:10 Monday with 5:12 Thursday for $552; and 6:10 with 7:38 for $575. All are economy round trips and currently below the $670 allowance.
The $618 option doesn’t seem worth paying more for if the return is identical. Is there any practical benefit to the earlier outbound?

It gets you to Nashville 1 hour 35 minutes earlier, so you would likely reach the hotel around 7:30 p.m. instead of 9:00 p.m. Otherwise, it adds no schedule advantage for the workshop. It also gives you less time to reach MSP Monday after you become available.
Then narrow it to the 6:10 outbound. I’m deciding between getting home earlier Thursday and having more airport cushion.

The $552 round trip is the efficient choice: Monday 6:10–8:17 p.m., then Thursday 5:12–7:23 p.m. To protect that return, request the rideshare immediately at 2:30 and aim to leave Music Row by 2:40; a serious traffic delay would reduce the margin. The $575 round trip keeps the same Monday flight but returns Thursday 7:38–9:49 p.m., leaving more than four hours between the workshop finish and departure.
Keep both as finalists. Label the earlier return as the preferred option, but note the departure timing from the client site clearly. Don’t book yet.

Two finalists retained, with no booking made:

Preferred — $552 round trip: MSP–BNA Monday, April 19, 6:10–8:17 p.m.; BNA–MSP Thursday, April 22, 5:12–7:23 p.m. Leave the Music Row client site promptly at 2:30 p.m., request the ride immediately, and target arrival at BNA by 3:25 p.m.

More-buffer option — $575 round trip: the same Monday 6:10–8:17 p.m. outbound; Thursday 7:38–9:49 p.m. return. This adds $23 and arrives home 2 hours 26 minutes later, but provides substantially more protection against traffic or a late workshop release.

Both remain within the $670 economy airfare allowance.
